Update: My mailer ate one of Jarek's feedback mails...  Fixed the
parameter in netif_set_gso_max_size() to be u32
whitespace issue due to a patch import botch.  Changed the types from
u32 to unsigned int to be more consistent with other variables in the
area.  Also brought the patch up to the latest net-2.6.26 tree.
Update: Made gso_max_size container 32 bits
location of gso_max_size within netdev to be less hotpath.  Made more
consistent names between the sock and netdev layers
define for the max GSO size.

This patch adds the ability for device drivers to control the size of
the TSO frames being sent to them
column2: per TCP connection.  By setting the

column1: netdevice's gso_max_size value
column2: the socket layer will set the GSO

column1: frame size based on that value.  This will propogate into the TCP
layer
column2: and send TSO's of that size to the hardware.

column1: This can be desirable to help tune the bursty nature of TSO on a
per-adapter basis
column2: where one may have 1 GbE and 10 GbE devices

column1: coexisting in a system
column2: one running multiqueue and the other not

column1: This can also be desirable for devices that cannot support full 64 KB
TSO's
column2: but still want to benefit from some level of segmentation

column1: offloading.
